newsitem.title: JAPAN: KDD to cut int'l phone rates by average 5.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: KDD to cut int'l phone rates by average 5.1 pct.

text.p: Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd (KDD) said on Thursday that it plans to cut its rates for international phone calls by an average 5.1 percent.
KDD said it planned to implement the rate cut from November 23.

"The latest cut is aimed at strengthening KDD's international competitiveness ahead of the planned deregulation of leased lines and a drastic change in the international phone market," KDD president Tadashi Nishimoto told a news conference.
The rate reduction will slash KDD's sales by three billion yen in the 1996/97 business year, Nishimoto said.
If it had been in force for the full fiscal year, it would have translated into a 9.3 billion yen reduction in annual sales, Nishimoto said.
KDD will substantially cut call rates to Asian and Latin American countries, where demand is growing fast, Nishimoto said.
The charge for a daytime three-minute call to South Korea, for instance, will be cut to 560 yen from 610 yen.
